requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately on node1.
requirements.summary: The module was absent, the installed modprobe policy resolved to /bin/false, and an actual load attempt failed while the module remained absent.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after a reboot.
requirements.summary: Persistent modprobe and dracut policies were installed, the initramfs was rebuilt without the driver, and a real reboot changed the boot ID. After recovery, usb_storage remained absent and a new load attempt was rejected.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use a solution compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations show RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 unchanged. The implementation used the platform's existing modprobe and dracut facilities, with no package installation shown.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. usb-storage was blocked immediately and remained blocked following a directly observed reboot, while the operating-system release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol is coherent: node1 was healthy before restart, restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed, and it recovered running with no failed units, a writable root filesystem, persistent policy, and successful post-reboot enforcement.
limitations: No physical USB mass-storage hot-plug test was captured; enforcement was instead directly tested through actual modprobe attempts before and after reboot.

There was no application data or cluster workload in the stated single-node task to validate during restart; recovery evidence covers system health, root filesystem state, persistent configuration, and module behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary system mutation was identified: the policy files, initramfs rebuild, behavioral probes, and reboot all directly supported the requested outcome or mandatory restart evidence. However, three small evidence artifacts remained in /tmp: usb-storage-load.out from cmd-ff94944452784501, benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-cfd83b237b2d474d, and usb-storage-post-reboot.out from cmd-cbae273b18e4411e. They were not cleaned up. No failed services, new listening sockets, or package-health damage was observed.
